
# Assignment 2 - analysis of the platform users

The figures below are produced by `analysis.R` (run it with `make`).
This document reads the cleaned data table and discusses the results.

```{r}
# 1. look at how the traits are distributed
# 2. check whether values are missing or implausible
# 3. explore how different types of users compare.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)

platform_users <- read.csv(here("Data", "DataA2", "platform_users.csv"))
platform_users_clean <- read.csv(here("Data", "DataA2", "cleaned_platform_users.csv"))
```

## How the traits are distributed

```{r}
summary(platform_users_clean)
```

## Missing and implausible values

```{r}
# in raw dataset, user_id had 0 NAs
# platform users --> platform_users_clean showed 200 rows being deleted.
# 10 columns hold NAs with a maximum of 20 NAs each,
# so there are 2 NAs per individual column and no multiple NAs per row.

users_with_na <- platform_users %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), is.na))

summary_df <- tibble(
  stage = c("Raw", "Cleaned"),
  rows = c(nrow(platform_users), nrow(platform_users_clean)),
  rows_with_na = c(nrow(users_with_na), 0)
)
summary_df
```

```{r}
# no negative values in the two watch-time columns, so nothing implausible
platform_users_clean %>%
  filter(base_videos_watched_mean < 0 | base_videos_watched_sd < 0) %>%
  nrow()
```

```{r}
include_graphics(here("src", "Assignment2", "users_analysis", "visuals", "missing_comparison.png"))
```

## How different types of users compare

### Satiation decay by preference

```{r}
user_groups <- platform_users_clean %>%
  mutate(
    preference_group = case_when(
      pref_BeautyFashion > pref_Gaming ~ "Beauty/Fashion",
      pref_Gaming > pref_BeautyFashion ~ "Gaming",
      TRUE ~ "Neutral"
    )
  )

user_groups %>%
  group_by(preference_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_users = n(),
    mean_satiation = mean(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_satiation = sd(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_satiation = median(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
include_graphics(here("src", "Assignment2", "users_analysis", "visuals", "satiation_pref.png"))
```

There is no noticeable difference in satiation decay between the two groups,
so preferring one topic over the other does not have an impact on satiation.

### Beauty/Fashion preference vs videos watched

Is there a correlation between beauty/fashion preference and the amount of
videos watched?

```{r}
include_graphics(here("src", "Assignment2", "users_analysis", "visuals", "cor_beauty_video.png"))
```

No, there is no clear trend visible.

### Need for interaction, top 100 of each preference

Compare the top 100 pref_Gaming users against the top 100 pref_BeautyFashion
users, based on their need for interaction.

```{r}
include_graphics(here("src", "Assignment2", "users_analysis", "visuals", "beautyvsgaming.png"))
```

```{r}
# also visualise grade of preference to see if there is a connection
top_beauty2 <- platform_users_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(pref_BeautyFashion)) %>%
  slice(1:100) %>%
  mutate(group = "Top Beauty/Fashion2",
         preference_score = pref_BeautyFashion)

top_gaming2 <- platform_users_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(pref_Gaming)) %>%
  slice(1:100) %>%
  mutate(group = "Top Gaming2",
         preference_score = pref_Gaming)

top_users2 <- bind_rows(top_beauty2, top_gaming2)

ggplot(top_users2, aes(x = need_interaction, y = preference_score, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Top Beauty/Fashion2" = "#FF69B4", "Top Gaming2" = "#4169E1")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Need for Interaction vs. Preference Score\nTop 100 Beauty/Fashion vs Top 100 Gaming Users",
    x = "Need for Interaction Score",
    y = "Group-specific Preference Score",
    color = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 15),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray90")
  )
```

No connection between need for interaction and how strong the preference is.
